headline: Spatial and editing profiles link RNA turnover and regulation to brain pathology
label: Spatial Rna Regulation Landscapes
summary: Spatially resolved transcriptomic methods now quantify RNA turnover, editing, and 3D organization directly within tissue.
synthesis: The dominant thread is transcript-level resolution of RNA regulation, rather than chromatin-level integration. Spatial NT-seq maps RNA turnover kinetics across mouse brain, and machine learning relates these kinetics to mRNA stability features and their regulators. A repeat-aware pipeline quantifies A-to-I editing in mouse SINE B2 non-coding RNAs, identifying editing hotspots that rise early in amyloid beta pathology. SM3DD provides a segmentation-free approach to 3D spatial transcriptomics, computing standardised transcript-to-transcript distances in lung tissue. The inflammatome study is a cross-disease transcriptional program rather than a spatial method, deriving a 2,000-gene set and a 100-gene signature with a sample-wise score. Across the spatial and editing items, what is new is measurement of RNA turnover, editing, and 3D organization within tissue, extending readouts beyond expression abundance.
